title: Louis Armstrong fronts the Cotton Club band
summary: In 1930 Armstrong came to the coast alone and fronted the band; Brown calls him the most beautiful trumpeter he ever heard.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: He also hired bands from out of town. That were traveling, weren't they?
Did they play there at the same time that you did? Or did you --
-- alternate engagements or alternate sets, or how did it work?

Well, for awhile we had stars come in and they would play with our band -- with the house band. One of the first ones that I remember like that was Louis Armstrong. In 1930 Louis Armstrong came out to the coast -- he came by himself, and he fronted our band -- you know -- played the band.
And if anyone thinks they've ever heard Louis now, or later years, they should have heard Louis in 1930. The most beautiful trumpet player I've ever heard.

The only man that ever made me enjoy coming to work. Believe me, he was terrific. People came from Seattle, Washington, all up and down the coast to hear Louis. He not only played wonderfully, he sang with a style of all his own, and he was even beautiful to watch.
And he was phenomenal on his instrument.
Had you been familiar with his playing before he came out here?
Very little. I heard a few records. But it was nothing like hearing him in person. He just would amaze you. He just hypnotized you, he was so beautiful.
Who else came to the Cotton Club that you heard?
